questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is made up of dead cells?
questions.solution:
Cork cambium undergoes periclinal division and cuts off thick walled suberised dead cork cells towards outside and it cuts off thin walled living cells i.e., phelloderm on an inner side.

Xylem parenchyma is the only living component of xylem. Phloem is a living, complex permanent tissue where only Bast fibres are dead. Collenchyma is called as living, mechanical, simple permanent tissue.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the wrong statement in the context of heartwood.
options: Organic compounds are deposited in it
It conducts water and minerals efficiently
It comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls
questions.solution: Heartwood is physiologically inactive due to the deposition of organic compounds and tyloses formation, so this will not conduct water and minerals. Heartwood is the central cylinder found in tree trunks. Heartwood forms as the tree ages, and the inner xylem cells lose the capacity to transmit water. Heartwood tends to be darker in colour than sapwood since it is normally filled with various types of oils, dyes, and sugars. The primary function of heartwood is to provide adequate support to the tree.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The vascular cambium normally gives rise to
questions.solution: During secondary growth in Dicotyledonous plants, vascular cambium and extrasteler cambium contribute together. While the vascular cambium gives rise to secondary xylem and secondary phloem. Phelloderm is formed by cork cambium which is extrasteler cambium.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the case of Poriferans, the spongocoel is lined with flagellated cells called
questions.solution: Choanocytes (collar cells) form the lining of spongocoel in poriferans (sponges). Flagella in collar cells provide circulation to water in the water canal system. These distinctive cells line the interior body walls of sponges. These cells have a central flagellum that is surrounded by a collar of microvilli. Choanocytes are versatile cells. Their flagella beat to create the active pumping of water through the sponge, while the collars of the choanocytes are the primary areas where nutrients are absorbed into the sponge. Furthermore, in some sponges, the choanocytes develop into gametes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An important characteristic that Hemichordates share with Chordates is
questions.solution: Pharyngeal gill slits are present in Hemichordates as well as in Chordates. The notochord is present in Chordates only. Ventral tubular nerve cord is a characteristic feature of non-chordates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which among these is the correct combination of aquatic mammals?
questions.solution: Sharks and Trygon (sting ray) are the members of Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fish) while whale, dolphin and seals are aquatic mammals belong to class Mammalia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Viroids differ from viruses in having:
questions.solution:
Viroids are sub-viral agents as infectious RNA particles, without a protein coat.

Virus:- It is a small infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of other organisms. It is an obligate intracellular parasite which can reproduce only by invading and taking over other cells as they lack the cellular machinery for self-reproduction.

Viroids:- These are the smallest infectious pathogens known. These are subviral, smallest known agents of infectious disease. The term viroid was coined by T.O. Diener (1971) to describe the agent of the potato spindle tuber disease. There are some 25 viroids which vary in nucleotide sequence. These are spread by plant propagation through seeds and by manual mishandling with contaminated implements.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mycorrhizae are the example of:
questions.solution: Mycorrhizae are symbiotic relationships that form between fungi and plants. The fungi colonize the root system of a host plant, providing increased water and nutrient absorption capabilities while the plant provides the fungus with carbohydrates formed from photosynthesis. Mycorrhizal fungi encompass many major groups of the fungus Kingdom and in the past were divided into two non-evolutionarily related groups: the ectotrophic and endotrophic based upon the position of the fungal hyphae in relation to the tissues of a plants roots. Ectomycorrhizal fungi ensheath the root cells but usually do not penetrate them (extracellular). Endomycorrhizal fungi penetrate and enter the cells of a plant root

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following are found in extreme saline conditions?
questions.solution: Archaebacteria are able to survive in harsh conditions because of branched lipid chain in the cell membrane which reduces the fluidity of the cell membrane. Archaebacteria are the oldest organisms living on the Earth. They are unicellular prokaryotes and belong to the kingdom, Archaea. They were first discovered in 1977 and classified as bacteria. Most archaebacteria appear like bacteria when observed under the microscope. However, they are quite different from bacteria and eukaryotic organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which among the following are the smallest living cells, known without a definite cell wall, pathogenic to plants as well as animals and can survive without oxygen?
questions.solution: Mycoplasmas are smallest, wall-less prokaryotes, pleomorphic in nature. These are pathogenic on both plants and animals. Smallest cellular organism is Mycoplasma gellisepticum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for extracting energy from carbohydrates to form ATP?
questions.solution:
Mitochondria are rod-shaped organelles that can be considered the power generators of the cell, converting oxygen and nutrients into adenosine triphosphate (ATP). ATP is the chemical energy "currency" of the cell that powers the cell's metabolic activities through aerobic cellular respiration.

Ribosomes are involved in protein synthesis which is accomplished by mRNA and tRNA of the cells. Lysosomes help in digesting non-functional organelles. Chloroplasts also prepare ATP by cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation during photosynthesis.

options: codensation  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  nuclear membrane disassembly  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  crossing over  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  segregation  <math><mo>→</mo></math>  telophase

questions.solution:
The correct sequence of events during mitosis would be as follows

(i) Condensation of DNA so that chromosomes become visible occurs during early to mid-prophase.

(ii) Nuclear membrane disassembly begins at late prophase or transition to metaphase.

(iii) An arrangement of chromosomes at equator occurs during metaphase, called congression.

(iv) Centromere division or splitting occurs during anaphase forming daughter chromosomes.

(v) Segregation also occurs during anaphase as daughter chromosomes separate and move to opposite poles.

(vi) Telophase leads to the formation of two daughter nuclei.

The root tip contains the root apical meristem. Above the root tip, there is a multicellular root cap. Behind the root apical meristem, there is a zone of elongation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Fruit and leaf drop at early stages can be prevented by the application of
questions.solution:
Among the various types of growth promoters in plants, Auxins, Gibberellins and Cytokinins are most common and well characterized. The Auxin delay abscission of leaves and fruits at early stages. Whenever leaf or fruit fall occurs, the organ concerned stops producing auxin. However, it promotes abscission of order, mature leaves, and fruit. Abscision is a natural phenomenon of old parts. Primarily this is accomplished by Abscisic acid hormone (ABA). NAA prevents fruit drop in tomato; 2,4-D prevents fruit drop in Citrus.

Cytokinins are mainly involved in cell division. Gibberellins are mainly involved in stem internode elongation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The morphological nature of the edible part of coconut is
questions.solution:
The edible part of coconut is endosperm. Coconut water is free nuclear endosperm and the white kernel is the cellular endosperm.

Initially, the coconut is a nuclear liquid endosperm. it is a coenocytic liquid tissue with lots of rapidly dividing nuclei. At some point, gelification of the soil surrounding the nuclei occurs and cellular boundaries start to appear. These cells and nuclei start to settle down on the endothelium (inner lining of the integuments) and the cells divide to produce a columnar sort of a covering over it. This is what forms the characteristic of coconut meat. Development of the cellular endosperm is by coalescence of these deposited cells and nuclei at the antipodal end and continues towards the top. The cells right above the endothelium stay meristematic for a long time while the columnar cells on top of this meristematic layer grow radially inward.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A dioecious flowering plant prevents both:
questions.solution: When unisexual male and female flowers are present on different plants, the condition is called dioecious, and it prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. Autogamy or self-fertilization refers to the fusion of two gametes that come from one individual. Xenogamy is the fertilization of a flower by pollen from a flower on a genetically different plant. Geitonogamy is considered if a first flower is pollinated by the pollen of the second flower of the same plant. Cleistogamy is self-fertilization that occurs within a permanently closed flower.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Functional megaspore in an angiosperm develops into:
questions.solution: Megaspore is the first cell of the female gametophytic generation in angiosperm. It is formed from the megaspore mother cell by meiosis. Out of the four cells created, only one megaspore develops, and remaining three degenerates. The formation of the female gametophyte from a single functional megaspore is called as monosporic development. It undergoes three successive generations of free nuclear mitosis to form 8-nucleated and 7-celled embryo sac.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Attractants and rewards are required for:
questions.solution:
Insect pollinated plants provide rewards as edible pollen grain and nectar. While some plants also provide a safe place for deposition of eggs. Insect pollination is a form of pollination whereby pollen of plants, especially but not only of flowering plants, is distributed by insects. Flowers pollinated by insects typically advertise themselves with bright colours, sometimes with conspicuous patterns leading to rewards of pollen and nectar; they may also have an attractive scent which in some cases mimics insect pheromones.

Both hydrophily (water pollination) and anemophily (wind pollination) do not require rewarding flowers. Cleistogamous flowers are self-pollinated.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Flowers which have single ovule in the ovary and are packed into inflorescence are usually pollinated by
questions.solution: Wind pollination or anemophily is seen in flowers having a single ovule in each ovary, and numerous flowers packed in an inflorescence. Wind pollination is a non-directional pollination. Wind-pollinated flowers are small, non-scented and colourless.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Double fertilization is exhibited by:
questions.solution: Double fertilization is a characteristic feature exhibited by angiosperms. It involves syngamy and triple fusion. There are two male gametes, out of which one fuses with the egg nucleus (n + n) during syngamy. During triple fusion, the other male gamete fuses with the polar nuclei and forms triploid (3n) Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN).

Which of the following statements are correct?

(i) Centre of mass of a body always coincides with the centre of gravity of the body.

(ii) Centre of mass of a body is the point at which the total gravitational torque on the body is zero

(iii) A couple on a body produce both translational and rotational motion in a body.

(iv) Mechanical advantage greater than one means that small effort can be used to lift a large load.
questions.solution:
(i) Centre of gravity coincides with centre of mass for bodies when gravitational field is uniform (usually for bodies of small height).

(ii) Since the gravitational force can be assumed to be centred at the centre of gravity, so torque of gravitational force about the centre of gravity must be zero. In mechanics, usually we deal with the objects of small height for which torque of gravitational force about centre of mass will also be zero.

(iii) Couple produces only rotational motion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The hepatic portal vein drains blood to the liver from
questions.solution:
The hepatic portal system is found in all vertebrates. The flow of deoxygenated blood from the digestive and absorptive parts of the alimentary canal (especially from the intestine) to the liver before returning to the systemic circulation is called hepatic portal circulation. 

The blood which comes from the alimentary canal contains absorbed food such as glucose, amino acids. The excess of glucose is converted into glycogen and is stored in the liver for later use.

questions.q: Lungs are made up of air-filled sacs the alveoli. They do not collapse even after forceful expiration, because of:
questions.solution: The volume of air present in the lungs after forceful expiration is known as residual volume which prevents the collapsing of alveoli even after forceful expiration. The tidal volume (TV), about 500 mL, is the amount of air inspired during normal, relaxed breathing. The inspiratory reserve volume (IRV), about 3,100 mL, is the additional air that can be forcibly inhaled after the inspiration of a normal tidal volume. The expiratory reserve volume (ERV), about 1,200 mL, is the additional air that can be forcibly exhaled after the expiration of a normal tidal volume.

The lagging strand towards replication fork
The leading strand away from replication fork

questions.solution:
The DNA polymerase III molecule helps in the DNA fork to synthesize simultaneously the DNA. One of the strands, with proper orientation, functions as a leading strand for which the synthesis is continuous. The lagging strand is oppositely oriented and thus, DNA Pol-III synthesizes this in fragments called the Okazaki fragment. Each Okazaki fragment is synthesized by DNA polymerase at lagging strand in 5′→3′ direction. New Okazaki fragments appear as the replication fork opens further.

As the first Okazaki fragment appears away from the replication fork, the direction of elongation would be away from replication fork.

questions.q:
Which of the following statement is coorect?
(i) The rods contain a purplish-red protein called the rhodopsin.
(ii) The photopigments are embedded in the membrane discs of the inner segment.
(iii) Retinal is a derivative of vitamin A.
(iv) Light induces dissociation of the retinal from opsin resulting in changes in the structure of the opsin.
questions.solution:
The inner layer of an eye is the retina, and it contains three layers of neural cells — from inside to outside — ganglion cells, bipolar cells and photoreceptor cells. There are two types of photoreceptor cells, namely, rods and cones. These cells contain the light-sensitive proteins called the photopigments. The daylight (photopic) vision and colour vision are functions of cones and the twilight (scotopic) vision is the function of the rods. The rods contain a purplish-red protein called the rhodopsin or visual purple, which contains a derivative of Vitamin A.

Mechanism of Vision

The light rays in visible wavelength focussed on the retina through the cornea and lens generate potentials (impulses) in rods and cones. As mentioned earlier, the photosensitive compounds (photopigments) in the human eyes is composed of opsin (a protein) and retinal (an aldehyde of vitamin A). Light induces dissociation of the retinal from opsin resulting in changes in the structure of the opsin. This causes membrane permeability changes. As a result, potential differences are generated in the photoreceptor cells. This produces a signal that generates action potentials in the ganglion cells through the bipolar cells. These action potentials (impulses) are transmitted by the optic nerves to the visual cortex area of the brain, where the neural impulses are analysed and the image formed on the retina is recognised based on earlier memory and experience.

Carotene is the source of retinal which is involved in the formation of rhodopsin of rod cells.

questions.q: Alexander Von Humboldt described for the first time:
questions.solution:
Species–Area relationships: German naturalist and geographer Alexander von Humboldt while exploring the South American jungles, found that within a region species richness increased with increasing explored area but only up to a limit. The relationship between species richness and area turned out to be a rectangular hyperbola for a wide variety of organisms like angiosperm plants, birds bats and freshwater fishes. The relationship is a straight line on a logarithmic scale. It is mathematically expressed as:

S = CAZ

OR

log S = log C + Z log A

where,
S = Species richness
A = Area
Z = Slope of the line (regression coefficient)
C = Y–intercept
